title: Urban simulation: network resilience and retail location

network.label: London rail network
network.definition: Largest connected component: the number of stations in the largest remaining group connected by paths in the modelled graph.
network.caveat: Sequential removals are hypothetical stress tests. Centrality is recalculated after each removal. This is connectivity, not a forecast of actual passenger disruption, rerouting or congestion. The supplied graph includes Underground, Overground and DLR stations.

weighted_context.caveat: Different weighted measures use different definitions: degree sums flows, betweenness uses inverse-flow costs, closeness uses segment length.

retail.label: Havering supermarket location

walk.caveat: Residents assigned using snapped output-area centroids, not individual addresses. These are modelled catchments, not observed walking behaviour.

retail.caveat: A production-constrained model redistributes fixed origin demand. Results are comparative scenarios, not revenue or profitability forecasts. Brand, price, capacity, land and operating costs are outside the specification. Observed-versus-predicted agreement is modest.

provenance.process: Extracted saved notebook outputs and original GraphML topology. No model rerun, no figure digitisation. Coordinates rounded to millimetres for display.
provenance.pdf: CASA0002 Urban Simulation final_submission.pdf, pages1-19; same extracted text as supplied Summative_Draft (2).pdf.
notes: Targeted trajectories come from Part1 cell10, not prose approximations.
Random baseline is shown only as its recorded endpoint; intermediate means and SD are not exported in the notebook text.
Store scenarios from Part2 cell20; walking catchments from cell30.
The fit figure is squared Pearson correlation from the notebook helper, not a held-out or deviance R-squared.
